item.title: BMW tuner AC Schnitzer to shut down after almost 40 years
item.description: Legendary tuner AC Schnitzer to shut down after almost 40 years in business thanks to a range of factors like US tariffs and lengthy parts approval processes.

item.title: It’s been almost 50 years since Australia last rationed fuel… are we about to go there again?
item.description: Australia last rationed petrol in 1979 but the federal government has reassured the public rationing is off the table... for now.

item.title: Trent Nikolic: Now is the time to discuss why Australia is not fuel self-sufficient
item.description: With talk of fuel such as diesel hitting $4.00/litre, rationing taking effect, or supply drying up, now is the time for Australians to be demanding a return to fuel self-sufficiency... and asking what happened to a 90-day reserve.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric review: Back to the future for Merc’s medium electric SUV
item.description: With one eye on its past, Mercedes-Benz has reimagined the future with its all new GLC electric medium SUV.

item.title: Fully charge your EV in 11 minutes: New battery tech says goodbye lithium, hello sodium
item.description: Yet another battery breakthrough has been achieved, with claims that new sodium-ion battery chemistry is capable of fully charging in just 11 minutes.

item.title: 2026 Mazda CX-5: Third generation model priced for Australia
item.description: Now in its third generation, Mazda’s all-new CX-5 medium SUV will go on sale in July with a sharp starting price under $40,000 before on-road costs.

item.title: Leapmotor C10 Sports+ Special Edition: 440kW electric SUV launched
item.description: Leapmotor has added a new Sports+ special edition of the C10 electric mid-size SUV with a dual-motor drivetrain, new 800V architecture and side decals.

item.title: Australian distributor of Chinese electric carmaker Xpeng enters administration
item.description: ASIC documents show that administrators have been appointed to take control of TrueEV, the local distributor for Chinese electric automaker XPeng.

item.title: From the Wheels archive: The 1974 oil crisis – when driving on Sunday was banned and Australia had eight years of fuel reserves
item.description: Wheels' Peter Robinson was on the ground in 1974 when the oil crisis hit with driving banned on Sundays and car manufacturing slowed to a crawl.

item.title: New ‘mullet plates’ roll out for Chinese cars in Australia
item.description: Victoria introduces a new number plate format tailored to Chinese-built vehicles, reflecting the rapid rise of these models in the local market.
